allObjections.title: Registry validation breaks system
allObjections.detail: §6.4 Risk #1 for Agent #26 identifies that validateRoster() enforces exactly 25 agents, but the spec requires adding a 26th row. This creates a deployment-blocking race condition where the registry validation must be updated before Agent #26 can be added, risking system-wide breakage if not sequenced correctly.

allObjections.title: Dual-authority pattern untested at scale
allObjections.detail: Agent #26 §1 introduces dual-authority [recommend_only, auto_write_internal, requires_human_gate] at the primary-agent layer, which §6.3 admits is the FIRST agent to ship this way. The BaseAgent.guard() implementation for this pattern has no production precedent, creating systemic risk for Orchestra auto-admission.

allObjections.title: PII scrubbing incomplete for feedback
allObjections.detail: Agent #10 §6.4 Risk #1 mentions scrubCredentials() extension per CA-10-E.2, but the spec doesn't define how 'customer self-identified names' heuristic works. The 'My name is...' pattern is trivially bypassed, leaving PII exposure in customer feedback streams that flow to multiple downstream agents.

allObjections.title: Rubric files unspecified security hole
allObjections.detail: Agent #8 §6.4 Risk #1 states rubric content is 'not yet ratified' and §6.1 requires creating 5 new rubric files, but there's no specification of how these rubrics are loaded or validated. Dynamic rubric loading without signature verification creates code injection risk in the quality gate.

allObjections.title: Tamper-evidence limitations
allObjections.detail: Section 14.2 describes a tamper-evident log using a hash chain. However, it does not specify how the initial hash is secured or how the integrity of the hash chain is verified across distributed systems. This could lead to vulnerabilities if the initial hash is compromised or if there is no mechanism to verify the chain's integrity across different nodes.

allObjections.title: Agent #6 crawl decision ambiguity
allObjections.detail: In Section 6.4, there is ambiguity regarding how Agent #6 should handle partial ACE artifacts. The decision to supplement with its own crawl or accept partial input is not clearly defined, which could lead to inconsistent behavior and results.

allObjections.title: Rubric version drift risk
allObjections.detail: Section 6.4 of Agent #8 highlights the risk of rubric version drift, where changes to rubric files can alter scores for the same input, making historical comparisons difficult. This could undermine the reliability of trend analysis and governance decisions based on these scores.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case of failures or errors, which could lead to data inconsistencies and system instability. Specifically, §14.2 Tamper-evidence does not address how to handle hash chain breaks or corrupted logs.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Error Handling
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient error handling mechanisms, which could lead to system crashes or unexpected behavior. For example, §3.2 Input shape does not specify how to handle invalid or malformed input data.

allObjections.title: Inadequate Security Controls
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide adequate security controls, such as authentication and authorization mechanisms, to prevent unauthorized access or data breaches. Specifically, §7.1 Credential handling does not specify how credentials are stored or managed.

allObjections.title: Cost Governor Integration
allObjections.detail: The proposal mentions that Agent #23 is the sole canonical budget enforcement owner, but it does not specify how Agent #23 will integrate with the existing cost governance framework. This lack of detail could lead to budget overruns or improper budget allocations. The proposal should clearly define the interaction between Agent #23 and the cost governance framework, including how budget caps are enforced and how cost signals are emitted.

allObjections.title: Data Quality Gate Thresholds
allObjections.detail: The data quality gate thresholds are mentioned but not clearly defined for all agents. For example, Agent #8 and Agent #10 have different thresholds for data quality, but the proposal does not specify how these thresholds are determined or how they will be enforced. This lack of clarity could lead to inconsistent data quality across agents and potential halts in the pipeline.

allObjections.title: Rubric Versioning and Panel Ratification
allObjections.detail: The proposal mentions that rubric files must be Panel-reviewed before Agent #8 ships, but it does not specify how rubric versioning will be managed or how the Panel will ratify the rubrics. This lack of detail could lead to inconsistent scoring criteria and historical trend lines that become incomparable. The proposal should clearly define the rubric versioning process and the Panel ratification criteria.

allObjections.title: Topic Schema Compliance
allObjections.detail: The proposal mentions that cross-cluster topics will ship in the Cluster D §2.1.0 P0 patch commit, but it does not specify how topic schema compliance will be enforced. This lack of detail could lead to inconsistent topic schemas and potential integration issues. The proposal should clearly define the topic schema compliance process and how it will be enforced.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Rubric Ratification

allObjections.title: Potential LLM Cost Escalation
allObjections.detail: Agent #10 Monitor's final report generation involves processing large context, which may lead to unexpected cost escalations if not properly managed.

allObjections.title: Complex Dependency Management
allObjections.detail: Agent #26 Orchestra Research has numerous dependencies on other agents and external data sources, increasing the complexity of its integration and maintenance.

allObjections.title: Audit Log PII Scrubbing
allObjections.detail: §14.3 mentions PII scrubbing for customer-sourced content, but it's unclear if this scrubbing is applied to ALL audit log entries, including those generated by agents.  If not, sensitive information could inadvertently be logged and exposed to users with audit access.

allObjections.title: Agent #6 ACE Artifact Decision
allObjections.detail: §6.4 risk #3 for Agent #6 highlights the decision of whether to supplement a partial ACE artifact with its own crawl.  The spec doesn't explicitly define the criteria for making this decision, potentially leading to inconsistent behavior and suboptimal research briefs.

allObjections.title: Agent #8 Rubric Versioning
allObjections.detail: §6.4 risk #2 for Agent #8 mentions rubric version drift and the need for version pinning.  However, the spec doesn't detail the process for version bumping rubrics or the governance around approving rubric changes, potentially leading to uncontrolled rubric updates.

allObjections.title: Agent #10 Webhook Authentication
allObjections.detail: §6.4 risk #3 for Agent #10 mentions webhook authentication using shared secrets.  The spec doesn't specify how these secrets are managed, rotated, or protected, potentially leading to security vulnerabilities if secrets are compromised.

allObjections.title: Agent #26 Dual Authority Reversion
allObjections.detail: Cluster E for Agent #26 reverts the dual-authority charter, but the CEO re-disposition is only 'pending'. This creates uncertainty about the agent's core functionality and whether it can autonomously write admission decisions.

allObjections.title: Agent #6 ACE dependency risk
allObjections.detail: §3.1's soft dependency on Agent #21's crawl artifact creates silent degradation risk. If ACE produces partial results (e.g. 3/8 pages crawled), Agent #6's 'content-insufficient' block may trigger prematurely, halting valid assessments despite usable data.

allObjections.title: Agent #8 unratified rubrics
allObjections.detail: §6.4 risk #1 notes rubric files aren't Panel-ratified. The 5 dimension rubrics (uiUxRubric.js etc.) remain undefined in the spec, creating scoring inconsistency risks. §10.1's dimension list isn't sufficient operational guidance.

allObjections.title: Agent #26 registry validation gap
allObjections.detail: §6.2 requires modifying _registry.ts's validateRoster() from 25→26 agents, but no test coverage or migration plan is specified. Current code (line 550) hardcodes 25-agent check - a breaking change if not atomically fixed.

allObjections.title: Monitor PII scrub completeness
allObjections.detail: §7.2 extends scrubCredentials() per CA-10-E.2, but novel PII vectors (e.g. biometric data patterns, custom ID formats) aren't covered. Adversarial operators could exfiltrate data via creative feedback field abuse until detection heuristics update.

allObjections.title: Research blocks on partial crawl
allObjections.detail: In §4.3 and §6.4, Agent #6 is allowed to halt on `content-insufficient`, but the spec also says it may consume partial `aceArtifact` data from Agent #21. There is no clear decision rule for when partial crawl data is good enough versus when the agent should self-crawl, so the same run can oscillate between block and degraded output depending on incidental crawl coverage.

allObjections.title: Data-quality gate is underspecified
allObjections.detail: §5.5 Cluster B sets `bodyContentCharsMin: 1000` and an alternate `pageCountMin: 3`, but it also says `degrade-on-any` for ACE re-use and `hard-halt-on-any` elsewhere. Those rules conflict with the earlier promise that Research is the pipeline entry and should not fabricate; the agent can end up emitting a brief from thin evidence rather than reliably blocking, which weakens the gate’s meaning.

allObjections.title: Prompt-injection mitigation is incomplete
allObjections.detail: §6.4 calls out crawl-body prompt injection, but the mitigation only says to use a deterministic prefix and quote the body in a system block. That is not enough if the crawl artifact contains adversarial HTML, instruction-like text, or tool-output fragments, because the model can still be induced to extract or follow embedded directives during summarization.

allObjections.title: Cache and lineage mismatch
allObjections.detail: §4.3 says HotStore TTL is 24h and downstream consumers can replay from HotStore within 24h, but the same brief is also written to ColdStore lineage keyed by `runId`. The spec never defines how to reconcile a re-run after 24h, nor whether a new crawl invalidates a prior lineage row, so provenance and reproducibility can diverge silently.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Error Handling in Agent #6
allObjections.detail: Agent #6's §3.3 preconditions do not explicitly handle cases where `productId` is not found in `ProductRegistry` or `targetUrl` is invalid. This could lead to unexpected behavior or errors downstream.

allObjections.title: Lack of Specificity in Agent #8's Rubric Versioning
allObjections.detail: Agent #8's §6.4 risk mentions version-pinning rubric files, but the spec does not detail how version changes will be managed or communicated to operators, potentially causing confusion or inconsistent scoring.

allObjections.title: Over-reliance on Anthropic API in Agent #10
allObjections.detail: Agent #10's §7.1 relies heavily on the Anthropic API for sentiment classification without detailing a fallback strategy if the API is unavailable or rate-limited, which could halt the agent's functionality.

allObjections.title: §14.2 hash chain verification gap

allObjections.title: Tamper-evidence limitations
allObjections.detail: Section 14.2 describes a tamper-evident log using a hash chain. However, it does not specify how the initial hash is secured or how the system prevents unauthorized access to the hash chain itself, which could allow tampering with the log.

allObjections.title: Subjective readiness scoring
allObjections.detail: In Section 6.4 of Agent #9, the readiness scoring is noted as subjective and varies by industry. This could lead to inconsistent assessments and potential misalignment with actual market readiness, impacting the reliability of the GTM assessments.

allObjections.title: Cross-tenant aggregation ambiguity
allObjections.detail: Section 6.4 of Agent #12 highlights a risk of cross-tenant scope ambiguity. The proposal mentions 'flowai-only' scope, but the potential for multi-tenant aggregation without clear boundaries could lead to data privacy issues.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case of failures or errors, which could lead to significant disruptions in the system. Specifically, §14.2 Tamper-evidence does not address how to handle hash chain breaks or corrupted logs.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Security Controls
allObjections.detail: The security controls outlined in §7 of each agent spec are insufficient, as they do not provide adequate protection against potential threats such as data exfiltration or unauthorized access. For example, Agent #9's security controls do not address the risk of competitive-intel crawl prompt injection.

allObjections.title: Inadequate Testing
allObjections.detail: The testing strategy outlined in the proposal is inadequate, as it does not provide sufficient coverage of all possible scenarios and edge cases. Specifically, the acceptance criteria for each agent do not include negative testing or error handling.

allObjections.title: Ambiguous scope in §14.3
allObjections.detail: The retention policy in §14.3 mentions a 'full jsonb blocks' but does not specify what constitutes a 'jsonb block.' This ambiguity could lead to inconsistent interpretations and potential data loss.

allObjections.title: Incomplete error handling in §14.2
allObjections.detail: The hash-chain mechanism in §14.2 does not specify how to handle hash mismatches. If a hash mismatch is detected, the system should have a clear procedure for alerting administrators and potentially rolling back to a previous state.

allObjections.title: Lack of rollback mechanism in §3.2
allObjections.detail: The quarterly auto-update mechanism in §3.2 does not include a rollback path if the auto-update inserts a malicious adapter. This lack of a rollback mechanism poses a significant security risk.

allObjections.title: Unclear operational authority
allObjections.detail: The operational authority for Agent #9 is described as autonomous for ToolMenu dispatch within budget, but the specific budget limits and the consequences of exceeding these limits are not clearly defined. This could lead to unpredictable behavior and potential security risks.

allObjections.title: Incomplete input handling in Agent #23
allObjections.detail: Agent #23 does not specify how it handles cases where the cost-ledger is empty or incomplete. This lack of detailed input handling could lead to false positives or missed cost anomalies.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal lacks detailed testing plans and acceptance criteria for the new agents, which could lead to undetected bugs and issues in production.

allObjections.title: Complex Dependencies
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces complex dependencies between agents, which could lead to cascading failures and make debugging and maintenance more difficult.

allObjections.title: Security Risks
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not adequately address potential security risks, such as data exfiltration and unauthorized access, which could compromise sensitive information and system integrity.

allObjections.title: Audit Log Incompleteness
allObjections.detail: The GovernanceAuditLog (§14) doesn't capture all relevant actions, specifically those performed by the agents themselves. For example, the decision-making process of Agent #9 (GTM) isn't explicitly logged, only the final assessment. This makes auditing the agent's reasoning difficult.

allObjections.title: Reliance on LLMs
allObjections.detail: Several agents (e.g., #9, #11, #13) heavily rely on LLMs for decision-making. This introduces a black-box element, making it difficult to understand and debug the agent's behavior. The deterministic prompt strategy only mitigates, not eliminates, this risk.

allObjections.title: Cost Governor Scope
allObjections.detail: Agent #23 (Cost Governor) focuses on cost anomalies but doesn't address resource utilization anomalies (e.g., excessive memory usage). This leaves a gap in resource management, potentially leading to performance issues or instability.

allObjections.title: Potential for Feedback Loops
allObjections.detail: The interaction between agents, especially with the ProductSSOT, creates potential feedback loops. For example, Agent #3 (Self-Renewal) acts on issues reported by Agent #10 (Monitor), which in turn updates the ProductSSOT. This could lead to unintended consequences if not carefully managed.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Error Handling
allObjections.detail: The Cluster B data quality gate specifies different error handling strategies for different agents. Agent #13 (Self-Protection) is allowed to emit no envelope on empty edge-log batch, while other agents halt. This inconsistency makes the system harder to reason about.

allObjections.title: Subjective readiness scoring risks
allObjections.detail: Agent #9's GTM readiness scoring lacks enforceable default rubrics (§6.4 Risk 1). Per-product overrides without baseline standards could lead to inconsistent 'demo-ready' assessments across industries.

allObjections.title: Missing watermark spec blocks Phase 2
allObjections.detail: Agent #13's Phase 2 capabilities require a watermark specification that doesn't exist (§6.4 Risk 1). This creates a hard dependency that could indefinitely delay critical IP protections.

allObjections.title: Static tracker list decay
allObjections.detail: Agent #11's industry-trackers.json lacks update mechanisms (§6.4 Risk 2). Static allowlists will degrade as tracked sources change format/domains, reducing discovery effectiveness over time.

objections.detail: The GovernanceAuditLog in §14.1 logs 17 distinct topics including low-signal events like 'w03_self_audit_*'. This creates log bloat (365-day hot retention) and increases attack surface for tampering. Specific risk: 'panel_decision_*' topics could leak sensitive deliberation patterns through metadata correlation.

objections.title: Agent #14 §6.4 Risk #1
objections.detail: The legal-counsel review process for LLM compliance assessments is undefined in implementation. §6.4 acknowledges this risk but provides no technical controls for audit trail of counsel review status, creating regulatory liability when 'legalCounselReviewStatus' field is manipulated.

objections.title: Agent #17 §5.4 Mode conflict
objections.detail: Agent #17's registry declares 'cross-step' mode while blueprint specifies 'always-on'. §5.4 notes unresolved conflict affecting OrchestratorHub wiring. Worse, Cluster C integration assumes mode-agnostic output but Locked Rule 16 requires mode-aware framing in Self-Renewal Alerts.

objections.title: Agent #20 §6.4 Carbon source risk
objections.detail: Carbon emission factors lack authoritative source (G20-Q1). Static tables (§6.1) ignore regional/time variations, causing misestimated ESG thresholds. When paired with §8.2's deferred real-time tracking, this creates false compliance confidence during carbon-intensive periods.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: During regulatory surge (e.g., simultaneous GDPR amendment + California CPRA update), Agent #14's annual tracker cadence (§3.2) misses critical changes. False 'compliant' assessments trigger auto-admission of non-compliant Orchestra candidates via §8.1 carve-out flags, creating regulatory penalties that manual monitoring would have prevented.
adversarial.precedent: no precedent known

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The collective dependency graph – Agent #14 requiring #11 SHIPPED-GREEN, #17 requiring #15/#26/#8 GREEN, and #18 requiring #11/#12/#17 GREEN – creates critical path risk. If any upstream agent underperforms, these new agents will emit high-confidence but low-fidelity outputs (e.g., §3.3 data quality gates degrade). Deferring until upstream agents demonstrate 90-day stability in production would prevent cascading misinformation.

A-14.rationale: Resolved counsel-review via §4.2 status field, but §6.4 risk #1 (process undefined) and G14-Q2 (annual tracker cadence) require non-blocking tracking in dispatch.

A-17.rationale: Mode conflict resolved via G17-Q1(c) in spec, 60-day evidence window (§6.4) addresses deprecation false positives, and 3-mode-path enforcement is schema-backed.

A-16.rationale: G16-Q1 scope ambiguity remains: §8.1 claims 'flowai-only' but §3.2 includes productScope parameter implying configurability. Must reconcile before wire-in to prevent tenant boundary violations.

A-18.rationale: Topic canonicalization complete but ±15% drift threshold (§8.1) lacks volatility adjustment. Track in dispatch as non-blocking given §9.6 baselineConfidence flag exists.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Objections emphasize systemic risks from topic sprawl (§14.1) and upstream dependencies. Steelman highlights valid critical-path concerns but ratification with conditions balances progress vs risk.

objections.title: Public Policy overstates legal safety
objections.detail: In §2, §4.2, and §10 G14-Q1, the agent still turns LLM-generated judgments into operator-facing compliance scorecards and same-day alerts. Saying the outputs are “advisory” does not solve the core hazard: the system may be operationally relied on as if it were legal advice, especially when it gates Orchestra auto-admission in §2 and §5.3.

objections.title: Tracker curation is a hidden legal surface
objections.detail: §3.1, §3.3, and §6.4 put `regulatory-trackers.json` under Panel/legal-counsel review, but the file is still an allowlist that defines what the company monitors. If the allowlist is stale or incomplete, the agent can create false reassurance by missing a regulator update in a jurisdiction the product actually touches.

objections.title: Carve-out gate can deadlock growth
objections.detail: §2 and §9 AC-14.2/AC-14.4 make joint carve-out flags a gating mechanism for Orchestra auto-admission, yet §8.3 says the agent can never remove products or auto-act. That combination risks a one-way ratchet where ambiguous or partial signals block admission indefinitely without a clear escalation/override path beyond human review.

objections.title: English-only scope is brittle
objections.detail: §8.2 defers multi-language tracking, but §9 AC-14.1/AC-14.5 already require meaningful coverage of GDPR-relevant and injection-resilient content. For regulators like CNIL, ICO, or member-state sources that publish nuanced updates in local languages, English-only crawling can miss the authoritative text or distort meaning in translation.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If a regulator updates a jurisdiction-specific rule in a non-allowlisted or non-English source, the agent may continue emitting a green or caveat assessment while the company assumes it is covered. That is worse than the status quo of no automated policy radar, because it creates a false sense of compliance and can delay counsel involvement until after the risky change has already propagated into admissions or product decisions.
adversarial.precedent: OpenAI and other LLM systems have repeatedly been tripped up by prompt-injection and source-document trust issues; this is a well-known failure mode in retrieval/crawl pipelines. More specifically, security researchers have shown “indirect prompt injection” in browsed content can steer downstream model outputs, which is directly analogous to §6.4 risk #4.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring this proposal is that it packages a genuinely legal-risky workflow as an operational agent. Even with disclaimers, the combination of crawl-based legal interpretation, advisor labeling, same-day alerts, and admission gating can be misunderstood as authoritative, and any miss creates compliance exposure. A narrower design that only records tracker deltas for counsel review, without scoring, gating, or operator-facing summaries, would be safer and easier to validate.

A-14.pick_text: RATIFY-WITH-CONDITIONS — v2 resolves the main prior conditions but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (non-blocking; specify in rationale).
A-14.rationale: The v2 spec fixes the most obvious prior gaps with advisory-only language and a counsel-review queue, so it is not a full rewrite case. But the remaining legal-authority and allowlist-coverage risks are material enough that they should be tracked as conditions, not ignored.

A-17.pick_text: RATIFY-WITH-CONDITIONS — v2 resolves the main prior conditions but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (non-blocking; specify in rationale).
A-17.rationale: The mode-canonicalization and 3-path framing are mostly cleaned up, but there is still residual ambiguity around always-on versus cross-step scheduling and deprecation false positives. That makes it suitable for conditional ratification rather than a clean promote.

A-16.pick_text: RATIFY — v2 cleanly resolves the prior Panel REVISE conditions; spec is ready for Wave 1 engineering wire-in.
A-16.rationale: This version meaningfully addresses the main privacy/scope concerns with `flowai-only`, aggregate-only reporting, and emit-boundary name rejection. The remaining risks are operational, but the design is now coherent enough to wire in.

A-18.pick_text: RATIFY-WITH-CONDITIONS — v2 resolves the main prior conditions but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (non-blocking; specify in rationale).
A-18.rationale: The spec is substantially tightened with drift thresholds, baseline confidence, and topic canonicalization, so the prior revision blockers are mostly addressed. I would still condition it on clearer override semantics for high-impact recommendations and more explicit validation of the drift baseline source.

A-20.pick_text: RATIFY-WITH-CONDITIONS — v2 resolves the main prior conditions but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (non-blocking; specify in rationale).
A-20.rationale: The three-tier carbon-factor policy substantially improves robustness over a single-source design and makes Phase 1 more defensible. Residual issues remain around source freshness and jurisdictional threshold ownership, so a conditional ratification is the safest vote.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The main concern across these specs is not implementation difficulty but overclaiming: several agents convert advisory analysis into workflow-shaping signals without strong enough guardrails. I voted for conditional approval where the design is coherent, and full ratification only where the privacy/scope boundaries are now actually enforceable.

objections.title: Lack of explicit error handling
objections.detail: §6.4 risk #4 in Agent #14 mentions prompt injection mitigation but doesn't specify error handling for LLM failures. Similar omission in Agent #17 §6.4 risk #3 and Agent #20 §6.4 risk #2.

objections.title: Inconsistent topic naming conventions
objections.detail: Agent #18 §4.1 produces '18.plan.update.v1' but implementation emits additional topics. Agent #20 §4.1 has similar issue. This inconsistency can lead to confusion and errors in downstream consumers.

objections.title: Dependence on external data sources
objections.detail: Agent #14 depends on 'regulatory-trackers.json' (§3.3) and Agent #20 depends on carbon-emission factors data source (§6.4 risk #1). These external dependencies can introduce reliability and security risks if not properly managed.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the LLM-generated compliance assessments in Agent #14 are not properly reviewed by legal counsel, they could lead to incorrect compliance decisions, making the system worse than the status quo by introducing legal risks.
adversarial.precedent: The failure of automated compliance systems in financial institutions due to lack of human oversight is a real-world precedent (e.g., Wells Fargo's automated compliance issues).

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest argument for rejecting or deferring the proposal is that the specifications for Agents #14, #17, #16, #18, and #20, while addressing some prior concerns, still contain significant risks and ambiguities that could lead to operational failures or legal issues if not properly addressed during implementation.

A-14.rationale: v2 resolves main prior conditions but surfaces residual issues like explicit error handling for LLM failures.

A-17.rationale: v2 addresses prior conditions but mode classification reconciliation (G17-Q1) remains a condition to track.

A-16.rationale: v2 resolves main prior conditions; however, the engineering dispatch should track the 'flowai-only' scope distinction codification (G16-Q1).

A-18.rationale: v2 addresses prior conditions; the engineering team should monitor the implementation of per-category drift thresholds (G18-Q2).

A-20.rationale: v2 resolves prior conditions; the carbon-emission factors data source decision (G20-Q1) should be tracked during implementation.

perReviewer.overallNotes: All agents' v2 specifications show improvement but require careful implementation and monitoring of residual issues.

objections.title: executorKey absent from §14.1 new topics
objections.detail: §14.1 cross-cutting rule requires every audit-log row from an executor to include executorKey, yet Agent #14 produces 14.regulation.new.v1 and 14.policy_assessment.v1 with no mention of executorKey population or fallback in §4.2 or §5.5 Cluster D.

objections.title: G17-Q1 mode options ignore runtime impact
objections.detail: Agent #17 §1 and §5.1 declare conflicting modes (cross-step vs always-on) while G17-Q1 options only address label reconciliation; none specify how daily 06:00 UTC vs monthly cadence changes OrchestratorHub wiring or Locked Rule 16 enforcement.

objections.title: Cluster F tier mismatch between #14 and #20
objections.detail: Agent #14 §5.5 Cluster F selects medium tier for dense regulatory text while Agent #20 §5.5 selects low tier; no cross-agent budget arbitration defined when both run in same monthly window against shared FLOWAI_MODEL_TIER_MEDIUM_FALLBACK_CHAIN.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Dormant agents with unresolved cross-references to unshipped executors and incomplete GovernanceAuditLog fields will emit partial or rejected envelopes, increasing alert noise and Panel review load beyond the current zero-agent baseline.
adversarial.precedent: no precedent known
